summary.topic: Solar-system objects and simplified flight planning
summary.learning_goal: Inspect planetary bodies and compare their displayed properties within a system view.
summary.primary_visualization: Solar-system overview and textured close views of Earth, Moon and Saturn.
summary.primary_interaction: Demo selects bodies and transitions the camera while updating property panels.

strengths: Named bodies have corresponding property panels, including radius and orbital period.
weaknesses: Displayed orbital and flight values are not independently validated; scales appear illustrative.

strengths: Overview-to-body navigation provides a route between system context and individual objects.
weaknesses: The recording does not demonstrate flight-plan consequences or explain the model assumptions in depth.

strengths: Textured body views and orbit paths make object identity and location legible.
weaknesses: Relative distances and size cannot be inferred as physically to scale.

strengths: Selection changes the active object, camera framing and data together.
weaknesses: The trip-planning control is visible but no completed plan change is shown.

strengths: Persistent navigation and property layout keep the view organized.
weaknesses: Three-column layout carries substantial small text; mobile behavior is unknown.

principles_to_learn: Link selected objects, camera and property panels.
Keep an overview route available while zoomed into one object.
Make simulation scale and simplification explicit.
things_not_to_copy: Do not turn approximate travel estimates into unqualified scientific facts.
Do not award untested trip-planning controls full interaction credit.
golden_recommendation: Provisional demo reference. Use for object selection, linked views, camera transition. Live behavior remains unverified.
